concepts.label: ethernet-service
concepts.gloss: A provider-delivered logical Layer 2 Ethernet connectivity service that associates two or more UNIs and transports customer Ethernet traffic between them according to a defined connectivity pattern.
concepts.example: ACME-ELAN is a multipoint Ethernet service connecting UNI-HQ, UNI-DC, and UNI-Branch with any-to-any forwarding.

concepts.label: UNI
concepts.gloss: A User Network Interface is the service access and demarcation interface at which a customer network attaches to a specific Ethernet service.
concepts.example: UNI-HQ is the ACME-ELAN access interface through which the headquarters customer equipment sends and receives service traffic.

concepts.label: EVC-endpoint
concepts.gloss: An EVC endpoint is the logical termination of an Ethernet service at a particular UNI, distinct from the physical or logical access interface itself.
concepts.example: EP-HQ represents ACME-ELAN's service termination at UNI-HQ, while EP-DC and EP-Branch represent its terminations at the other UNIs.

concepts.label: network-segment
concepts.gloss: A network segment is a customer-visible Layer 2 broadcast domain, commonly identified by a VLAN, whose Ethernet frames are transported by the Ethernet service.
concepts.example: CE-VLAN 200 is carried across ACME-ELAN so devices attached through its three UNIs participate in the same customer broadcast segment.

concepts.label: bandwidth-profile
concepts.gloss: A bandwidth profile is a set of traffic-rate limits and associated metering behavior applied to Ethernet traffic at a UNI.
concepts.example: BWP-200/50 applied at UNI-HQ meters traffic there using its configured 200/50 rate parameters, whereas BWP-100/0 represents a different rate allocation.

concepts.label: class-of-service
concepts.gloss: A class of service is a named traffic category on an Ethernet service that selects a distinct forwarding priority or performance treatment.
concepts.example: On ACME-ELAN, delay-sensitive traffic is assigned to CoS-H for real-time treatment, while ordinary traffic is assigned to best-effort CoS-L.

concepts.label: MAC-learning
concepts.gloss: MAC learning is the Layer 2 control behavior at a UNI that learns source MAC addresses from ingress frames and associates them with that attachment for subsequent forwarding decisions.
concepts.example: With dynamic learning enabled at UNI-HQ, a frame arriving from a headquarters device causes its source MAC address to be learned against UNI-HQ.

concepts.label: service-mtu
concepts.gloss: The service MTU is the maximum Ethernet frame size that the Ethernet service is specified to accept and carry without exceeding its framing limit.
concepts.example: An MTU of 9100 means ACME-ELAN is provisioned to carry Ethernet frames up to 9,100 bytes under the model's frame-size convention.

concepts.label: service-availability
concepts.gloss: Service availability is the assurance objective specifying the proportion of an observation period during which the Ethernet service is expected to be operational and usable.
concepts.example: A 99.99% availability objective requires ACME-ELAN to meet that uptime percentage over the SLA's defined measurement period.

concepts.label: x-mef-attr-5
concepts.gloss: x-mef-attr-5 is an opaque proprietary UNI-scoped configuration attribute whose operational meaning is vendor-defined rather than specified by the standard service model.
concepts.example: At UNI-HQ, x-mef-attr-5 is set to hexadecimal value 0x3, which must be interpreted using the supplying vendor's documentation.
